newsitem.title: UK: BZW strategists extend lead in fund manager poll.
newsitem.headline: BZW strategists extend lead in fund manager poll.

text.p: Richard Kersley and his team at BZW extended their lead as top-rated UK equity strategists in the 1997 Reuters fund managers poll, the annual survey showed on Tuesday.
Kersley and colleagues Steve Wright and Robert Barrie came top with a vote of 18.5 percent, weighted to reflect the size of funds under management, up from 16.8 percent last year.
The NatWest Securities team led by Bob Semple moved up into second place with a score of 15.9 percent, from third last year, according to the survey compiled by Tempest Consultants.
Merrill Lynch's team led by Philip Wolstoncroft moved up to third from fifth.
BZW's Kersley said his team's approach was based on taking overall market and economic views and relating that to trends in individual stocks and sectors.

"The key point from our point of view is making macro economic issues relevant on a company level," Kersley said. "What strategy should be all about is building a bridge between the top-down and bottom-up views."
Kersley admitted BZW had been too upbeat on industrial company shares in recent months, having failed to predict the impact of continuing sterling strength.
But he claimed a success in last year predicting the underperformance of retail shares, despite rising consumer confidence. "We were bearish of retail stocks at the right time," he said.
The complete ranking for UK equity strategists was as follows:
5 ABN AMRO Hoare Govett 9.25 pct 12.12 pct
